docs.title: Cobblemon Raid Icons
docs.text:
Raid dens are easy to walk past and impossible to find again. This draws every one of them on your map as its tera type icon — on the minimap and the world map alike — so the fire den you wanted is one glance away, and the six you don't want stay out of the way.

It runs entirely on your client. The server never needs to know you have it.

MC 1.21.1 Fabric NeoForge Client-only Needs Raid Dens

Get started The icons

docs.title: What can it do?
docs.text:
• Icons on both maps — the den's tera type, drawn on Xaero's minimap and on the world map.
  • A tooltip that names the den — hover a den on the world map for the Pokémon waiting in it, its star tier and its tera type.
  • A den clock — how long until the den rolls a new raid or comes back, exact in your own world and estimated on a server.
  • Filters and icon sizes — hide the tiers you have outgrown, the types you are not hunting, and the dens that are not active, and size the icons per map.
  • /raidicons — the settings screen, every setting from chat, and a report that says what the mod can see when a den is not showing up.

docs.title: Get it
docs.text:
Download Modrinth · What changed Version 3.0.0 Minecraft 1.21.1 Side Client only. It goes in your own mods/ folder; a server does not need it Cobblemon Cobblemon Raid Dens brings it with it Also needs Cobblemon Raid Dens Fabric Fabric API, Fabric Language Kotlin NeoForge Kotlin for Forge Optional Xaero's Minimap: the icons on the minimap · Xaero's World Map: the icons on the world map · Cloth Config: the settings screen (with Mod Menu on Fabric)

New here? Start with Getting Started.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
One command, and it runs entirely on your client — it is never sent to the server, so it works everywhere, including on servers where you have no permissions at all. It works the same on Fabric and NeoForge.

Command What it does /raidicons Opens the settings screen. /raidicons report Prints what the mod can currently see — the first thing to run when a den is not showing up. /raidicons config Lists every setting with its current value. /raidicons config <setting> Shows one setting, with its range and its default. /raidicons config <setting> <value> Changes a setting. /raidicons config reset [<setting>] Restores one setting to its default, or all of them. /raidicons config teraTypes add <type> · remove <type> Shows or hides one tera type without retyping the whole list.

docs.title: /raidicons
docs.text:
Opens the settings screen, in any world, with no trip back to the mod list. The screen needs Cloth Config: without it the command says so and points you to /raidicons config, which changes every setting from chat.

The same screen has a key. Under Controls, the Cobblemon Raid Icons heading has an Open settings key. It starts unbound, so it never collides with Xaero's keys; bind it once and it opens the screen from anywhere in game.

docs.title: /raidicons config
docs.text:
Every setting in Configuration can be read and changed from chat, with no Cloth Config needed. A change is saved to the file and shows on the map straight away, with no restart.

/raidicons config                      → lists every setting and its value
/raidicons config minTier              → minTier = 0 (0-7, default 0)
/raidicons config minTier 5            → minTier = 5
/raidicons config reset minTier        → minTier = 0
/raidicons config reset                → every setting restored to its default

The tera filter takes the whole list at once, or one type at a time — and the command suggests the type names as you type:

/raidicons config teraTypes fire,dragon
/raidicons config teraTypes add water
/raidicons config teraTypes remove fire
/raidicons config teraTypes all

all clears the filter, so every type is shown again. The filter can never hide every type: removing the last one left is refused.

docs.title: /raidicons report
docs.text:
Reports what the mod can currently see. Run it while aiming at a raid den crystal: the most useful line it prints is what the game says that block actually is.

Raid Icons
  den block: cobblemonraiddens:raid_crystal_block
  layers: minimap=true worldmap=true
  scan: 4096 chunks examined, 3 den(s) known
  clock: 0 den(s) reading exactly, 2 reset span(s) measured
  nearest den: fighting tier 5 at 214, 71, -388 (36m) boss=klinklang_terafighting feature=NONE
  looking at: cobblemonraiddens:raid_crystal_block [raid_type=fighting, raid_tier=tier_five,
    is_active=true] - MATCHES the den block

Every line answers a different question, and together they narrow any "my dens aren't showing up" to one cause:

Line What it tells you den block Whether Raid Dens is installed at all. NOT in the registry means nothing can ever be found. layers Whether Xaero's minimap and world map were found. Both false means the mod has nowhere to draw. scan How much ground has been covered and how many dens are known. 0 chunks examined means the scan is not running. clock Where the den clock gets its numbers. In your own world, the dens reading their exact timer; on a server, how many resets the mod has timed so far — it needs two before it shows a countdown. nearest den The closest den the mod knows, with its type, tier, distance, boss and feature (NONE for an ordinary den). looking at The aimed block's registry id and every blockstate property it carries, verbatim — and whether the mod recognises it.

The report also goes to your log (logs/latest.log), so you can read it afterwards, or paste it into a bug report without having taken a screenshot at the right moment.

The line that matters

Everything this mod does rests on one assumption: that the crystal in front of you is the block and the properties it expects. looking at confirms or destroys that assumption in one step. If it says is NOT the den block while you are aiming at a den, that is the whole bug report.

docs.title: What the log shows
docs.text:
Without running anything, the mod writes three kinds of line to logs/latest.log, all starting with [Raid Icons]:

Line When What it rules out scan: N chunks examined, N den(s) known, player at … Every 10 seconds, only while no den is known. If the chunk count grows, the scan is running and simply has not met a den yet. den at … - <type> tier N active=… boss=… feature=… Once per den, the first time it is found. That den was found and read — if it is not on the map, a filter is hiding it. first draw: <layer> (N den(s) known) The first time each Xaero map asks the mod to draw. The layer is hooked into that map. No line for a map means Xaero never asked.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
There are three ways to change a setting, and they all edit the same file:

  • The settings screen, with Cloth Config installed.
  • /raidicons config from chat, with nothing else installed.
  • The file itself, described below.

A change made in game shows on the map as soon as it is saved, with no restart.

docs.title: The settings screen
docs.text:
With Cloth Config installed, the mod gets a settings screen. Open it with /raidicons, with the Open settings key under Controls (unbound until you set it), or from the mod list: the config button in Mod Menu on Fabric, and in NeoForge's own mod list.

It has three tabs: Filters (only active dens, lowest star tier, one switch per tera type), Icons (the two icon sizes) and Advanced (the scan). Without Cloth Config the button is simply not there, and the command and the file work as before.

docs.title: The file
docs.text:
The settings live in config/cobblemon_raid_icons.properties, inside your game folder — the same config/ your other mods write to. The file is created with the defaults the first time you load a world, so start it once and then edit it.

An unreadable or misspelled value never stops the mod: it falls back to its default and says so in the log.

scanRadius=12
chunksPerTick=12
onlyActiveDens=false
minTier=0
teraTypes=
minimapIconScale=100
worldMapIconScale=100

docs.title: The filters
docs.text: These decide which dens get an icon. They are the settings worth touching.

docs.title: minTier
docs.text:
The lowest star tier that gets a marker, from 0 to 7. 0 marks everything; a value outside that range is clamped to it.

Value Effect 0 Every den, whatever its tier. The default. 5 Only 5-star dens and above — the endgame view. 7 Only 7-star dens. Every feature den is 7-star, but so are many plain ones, so this does not single them out.

A den whose tier the mod could not read is always drawn, at any setting. It might be the one you want, and hiding it on a technicality is worse than one extra icon.

docs.title: teraTypes
docs.text:
The tera types that get a marker, comma-separated. Empty means all of them, which is the default.

# Only fire and dragon dens
teraTypes=fire,dragon

The names are the eighteen types plus stellar, lower-case:

normal · fire · water · electric · grass · ice · fighting · poison · ground · flying · psychic · bug · rock · ghost · dragon · dark · steel · fairy · stellar

An unrecognised name is dropped from the list rather than silently matching nothing.

A feature den is never hidden by this filter. Its marker shows the feature, not the tera type, so filtering it out by type would hide it for a reason the map does not show.

docs.title: onlyActiveDens
docs.text: true hides dens that are not currently live. Default false, which draws every den whether it is ready to fight or resetting.

docs.title: minimapIconScale and worldMapIconScale
docs.text:
How big the den icons are, as a percentage of each map's normal size. Default 100, clamped to 50–200 — from half to twice the size.

There is one per map so you can shrink a crowded minimap without making the world map harder to read. At 100 an icon is 36×36 pixels on the minimap and 48×48 on the world map.

docs.title: The scan
docs.text: The two remaining settings control how the mod looks for dens. The defaults are good; change them only if you have a reason.

docs.title: scanRadius
docs.text:
How many chunks out from you are examined. Default 12, clamped to 1–32.

Raising it past your render distance buys nothing: chunks the game has not loaded hold no dens as far as this mod is concerned.

docs.title: chunksPerTick
docs.text:
How many chunks are examined each client tick. Default 12, clamped to 1–64.

The scan cycles continuously over the whole radius, so this sets how quickly a newly placed den appears — at the default, the full radius comes round in under three seconds. Each chunk is nearly free to check, so there is little to gain by lowering it.

docs.title: Checking a change took effect
docs.text: Run /raidicons report. The scan line shows the ground actually being covered, and the nearest den line shows what survived your filters.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
Cobblemon Raid Icons is client-side. It goes in your own mods/ folder and nowhere else: the server does not need it, does not know you have it, and cannot tell the difference. Play on any server that runs raid dens.

Drop one jar — the one for your loader, never both.

FabricNeoForge Minecraft 1.21.1 Required Fabric API · Fabric Language Kotlin Required Cobblemon Raid Dens (CurseForge) For the icons Xaero's Minimap and/or Xaero's World Map Minecraft 1.21.1 Required Kotlin for Forge Required Cobblemon Raid Dens (CurseForge) For the icons Xaero's Minimap and/or Xaero's World Map

Optional: Cloth Config adds a settings screen, and on Fabric Mod Menu puts its button in the mod list. Without them every setting still changes with /raidicons config.

Cobblemon Raid Dens brings Cobblemon and GeckoLib with it, so you do not install those separately for this mod's sake.

One Xaero is enough

Install the minimap alone and you get icons on the minimap. Install the world map alone and you get icons and tooltips on the big map. Install both and you get both. With neither, the mod loads and quietly draws nothing.

docs.title: What you should see
docs.text:
Walk into a world with raid dens in it. Within a few seconds of a den's chunk arriving, its tera type icon appears where it stands — a fire den shows the Fire icon, a stellar den the Stellar one.

The mod only knows about dens in chunks the game has already sent you, so icons fill in as you walk. Teleporting across the map and expecting it to be covered in markers is the one thing that looks broken and is not: there is nothing loaded out there to find.

Open the world map and hover a den to see what is waiting in it and when it next resets.

To hide the dens you do not want, run /raidicons for the settings screen, or /raidicons config to change settings from chat.

docs.title: When nothing shows up
docs.text: Run /raidicons report while aiming at a den crystal. In one screen it tells you whether the den block is in the registry, whether Xaero's layers were found, how much the scan has covered, and what the game says the block in front of you actually is.

docs.title: The Icons
docs.text:
Every raid den the mod has seen is drawn where it stands, as the icon of its tera type — or, in a Dynamax, Gigantamax or Mega raid, as the icon of its feature. A den is found the moment its chunk reaches your client, and the marker disappears the moment the crystal does — mine one and it is gone from the map on the same tick.

The markers are not waypoints. They are drawn by the mod straight onto Xaero's maps, so they never enter your waypoint list, cannot be dragged out of place, and leave nothing behind when you uninstall.

docs.title: Tera icons
docs.text:
A den is drawn as its boss' tera type, one icon for each of the eighteen types and one for Stellar.

Normal Fire Water Electric Grass Ice Fighting Poison Ground Flying Psychic Bug Rock Ghost Dragon Dark Steel Fairy Stellar

docs.title: Feature dens
docs.text:
In a Dynamax, Gigantamax or Mega raid, the tera type is not what you are choosing — the raid itself is. A marker that showed the type would be showing the wrong fact, so those dens are drawn as their feature instead:

Icon Drawn for Tooltip colour Dynamax, Eternamax Red for Dynamax, purple for Eternamax Gigantamax Magenta Mega, Mega X, Mega Y Blue

Eternamax shares the Dynamax icon: it is the same raid dressed differently, and rare enough that a third icon would mostly go unseen.

Every other den keeps its tera icon, and that includes Tera, Shadow, Primal and Stellar raids — in those, the type genuinely is the point.

A den's star tier says nothing about whether it is featured. Every featured den is 7-star, but so are many plain ones, so the mod reads the feature from the boss itself.

docs.title: On the minimap
docs.text:
The icon sits over the minimap at 36×36 pixels — big enough to read at a glance in the corner of the screen, small enough that a cluster of dens does not bury the terrain. If your minimap is crowded, minimapIconScale shrinks it, down to half.

Every marker fills the same space, whichever icon it is: a Stellar den next to a Fire den, or a Mega den next to either, reads as an equal marker.

A den that is outside the minimap's view is not drawn at all. Xaero pins an off-view marker to the rim of the minimap, which is the right behaviour for a waypoint you chose to watch and the wrong one for every den in the world: the border would fill up with icons for dens hundreds of blocks away.

docs.title: On the world map
docs.text: The same icon, at 48×48 — the world map is a whole screen, and an icon sized for the minimap reads as a speck on it. worldMapIconScale changes it on its own, without touching the minimap.

docs.title: The tooltip
docs.text:
Hover a den on the world map and it names itself, says when it next changes, and explains what that means:

Klinklang
★★★★★ Fighting
New raid in 12m
Open: every reset rolls a new raid here.

The Pokémon waiting in the den comes first, because that is what you are deciding on. Below it, the star tier and the tera type, written in that type's own colour. Then, in grey, the den clock and a line on the den's life cycle.

A feature den names its feature in the second line instead, in the feature's colour, and keeps its clock like any other den:

Alcremie
Gigantamax
New raid in 12m
Open: every reset rolls a new raid here.
Featured raid: shows its feature, not a tera type.
The tera type filter never hides it.

The feature replaces both the stars and the type rather than joining them: the type is not what the raid is about, and every featured den is 7-star anyway. The last two lines say why the tera filter leaves it on the map.

A den that has been beaten says so, and points at the filter that hides dens like it:

Klinklang
★★★★★ Fighting
Back in 12m
Beaten: back with a new raid at the next reset.
"Only active dens" hides beaten dens.

If your client has not yet received the den's contents, the species line is left out rather than filled with a placeholder. A tooltip that said "Unknown" would be claiming the den has no boss, which is a different fact from not knowing yet.

docs.title: The den clock
docs.text:
A den runs one clock: its reset. When the reset comes, an open den rolls a new raid in the same spot, and a beaten den comes back with one. Both count down to that same moment, so the tooltip reads New raid in for an open den and Back in for a beaten one.

How exact the number is depends on where you play:

The tooltip says When New raid in 12m · Back in 4m Exact. In your own world, or as the host of a LAN game: your game is also the server, so the den's real timer is read straight off it. Open for 3m · Down for 3m On someone else's server, before the mod has timed enough resets to know how long the cycle is. It says only what it has seen: how long the den has been in its current state. New raid in ~12m · Back in ~4m On a server, once the mod has watched dens reset at least twice. The ~ marks it as an estimate. New raid due (~40m on this one) · Due (~40m down) The estimate has run out and the den has not reset yet. Rather than count below zero, it says the reset is due.

On a server there is nobody to ask: Raid Dens keeps the timer to itself and sends your client the raid boss and nothing else. So the mod measures the cycle by watching dens turn over while you are near them. A den you walk away from and come back to an hour later teaches it nothing, because it cannot tell when the change happened while you were gone.

The clock never decides what is drawn. A den whose time runs out is not gone — it rolls a new raid in the same place — so it stays on the map.

docs.title: The right-click menu
docs.text: Right-click a den on either map and Xaero's menu is titled by the same rule as the icon: Fighting Raid Den for an ordinary den, Gigantamax Raid Den for a featured one.

docs.title: What gets an icon
docs.text:
Everything the scan finds, until you say otherwise. Three filters narrow it down:

  • Star tier — hide everything below the tier you are hunting.
  • Tera type — list the types you care about and the rest stop being drawn. A feature den is never hidden by it, because its marker does not show a type.
  • Active only — hide the dens that are not currently live.

A den whose tera type the mod does not recognise still gets a marker. A den you cannot classify is worth more on the map than no den at all.

docs.title: Why icons appear as you walk
docs.text:
The mod reads dens out of the chunks your game has already been sent — it asks the server for nothing and adds no network traffic. Chunks you have never loaded hold no dens as far as it is concerned, so the map fills in behind you as you explore rather than all at once.

That also means a den someone else builds far away appears the next time you are near it, and the scan re-checks what it knows continuously, so a den that changes is never remembered wrong.

A den you walked away from stays on the map, drawn as it was when you last saw it, even after its raid should have reset — it rolls a new raid in the same spot, so the crystal is still there. It is updated the next time you come near it, and it leaves the map only when its crystal is gone.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Common surprises, what causes them, and what to do. If yours is not here, post it in the Discord: it files the ticket for you.

docs.title: No icons show up
docs.text: Run /raidicons report while aiming at a den crystal. In one screen it tells you whether the den block is in the registry, whether Xaero's layers were found, how much the scan has covered, and what the game says the block in front of you actually is.

docs.title: Icons only on the minimap, or only on the world map
docs.text: Each Xaero mod carries its own icons. The minimap alone gives icons on the minimap; the world map alone gives icons and tooltips on the big map; both give both. With neither, the mod loads and quietly draws nothing.

docs.title: Icons appear only as I walk
docs.text: The mod can only find dens in ground your game has loaded. See Why icons appear as you walk.

docs.title: There is no settings screen
docs.text: The screen comes from Cloth Config, and on Fabric its button from Mod Menu. Without them every setting still changes with /raidicons config.

docs.title: Do I install it on the server?
docs.text: No. Raid Icons is client-side: it goes in your own mods/ folder and nowhere else.
